title: chats-blob — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_chats_blob_raw + protocol::decode_chats_blob — the MYJ1 per-conversation chats-file codec (myne-md/myne#675). Each conversation file is sealed under the family chats_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::ChatsKey), with conversation_id (16 B) + account_number_hash (16 B) bound via aad_chats_blob (the MYE1 per-entry archetype: one KEK serves every file). The inner plaintext is the client layer's canonical turn-list payload JSON ({title_derived_from, turns}); the codec treats it as opaque bytes. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output, incl. the create-state payload and a frozen-proposal payload), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4, incl. the cross-conversation-id refusal the per-entry binding owes), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per ChatsBlobError variant). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/chats_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.24 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'chats-blob/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives chats_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::ChatsKey, role string 'chats-key') before calling the encoder.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 55-byte AAD via aad_chats_blob (role string 'chats-blob').

input_conversation_id_hex.description: 16-byte conversation id (hex). Bound into the AAD in the per-entry position, so a blob sealed for one conversation fails to verify as another.

input_plaintext_hex.description: Canonical turn-list payload JSON bytes (hex): {title_derived_from, turns}. The codec treats these bytes as opaque.

input_blob_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_chats_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::ChatsKey). Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_blob_hex assertion.

expected_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: Recovered turn-list payload bytes (hex). The decoder returns these for the sync layer to parse into turns.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: ChatsBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault vs cross-conversation vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / format / length checks all run before the AEAD stage (§9.24.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: ChatsBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, FormatUnsupported, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated, CiphertextLenOverflow}). Unlike the AEAD failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are pre-decryption and intentionally distinguishable.
